question: Will a non-MF group be proved this month?
resolution_criteria:
Specifically, will before September 2026, will there be a proof of a finitely presented discrete MF group?

If so, this would negatively resolve a long-standing open question about if all groups are MF.

This was described as a major open problem in group theory, and a “holy-grail” alongside two other questions.

GPT 5.6 Sol says the question is equivalent to: “Can every countable group be faithfully approximated by finite-dimensional unitary matrices when the approximation error is measured in operator norm?”

This question resolves YES if a proof is given this month and is generally considered valid. If it takes longer than August to verify but the proof was written in August, it still resolved YES.

If all groups are MF, this resolves NO. If no valid proof from August comes about, this resolves NO.

I will bet on this market and have insider (publicly accessible) knowledge which leads me to believe the answer will be YES.
research:
**Will a non-MF group be proved this month? Research notes for the August 2026 window (as of 2026-10-04)**

Bottom line: at least two non-MF group constructions were found in mid-August 2026 and written up. I found no source that confirms either group is finitely presented, which the question's wording requires. My page fetches were mostly blocked (arXiv, Manifold and the blog refused the connection; GitHub returned 403), so the details below come from search snippets.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question is a Manifold market resolved by its creator, with no external data series. Two copies exist: [user496577185415897490191](https://manifold.markets/user496577185415897490191/will-the-existence-of-a-nonmf-group) and [SCS](https://manifold.markets/SCS/will-the-existence-of-a-nonmf-group). The criteria ask for a "finitely presented discrete MF group", which is presumably meant to say "non-MF". Proofs written in August count even if they are verified later.
- Undated (Aug 31 snippet): in the comments, one trader said "multiple different proofs publicly available online posted in August", and a skeptic asked where they were. The creator said they had not resolved the market yet so mathematicians could look for errors. I could not get the current price or confirm whether it has resolved, because the page would not load. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/user496577185415897490191/will-the-existence-of-a-nonmf-group)

## 2. Current status
- The existence of a non-MF group appears to be effectively settled by August 2026 work, which is the core claim. Whether either example is **finitely presented** is not confirmed in anything I could access.
- 2026-08 (arXiv 2608.28772): Caleb Eckhardt, "Non-MF groups and non-finite full group C*-algebras." He takes a property (T) group Γ that has an injective, non-surjective endomorphism, forms its ascending HNN-extension G, and shows the wreath-type group W = (⊕ Z/2) ⋊ G is not MF. Groups of this lamplighter-type kind are usually not finitely presented, but I could not check the paper. The acknowledgements say Scott Sauers also used ChatGPT to construct non-MF groups. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.28772)
- Sauers' GitHub repository contains `non_mf_groups_exist.tex`, which "proves that not every group is MF". There is also a Lean project listed on Reservoir. [GitHub](https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation), [Reservoir](https://reservoir.lean-lang.org/@SauersML/GroupApproximation/_payload.json)
- Issue #191 in that repository ("Final pre-arXiv pass ... Eckhardt situating ... Thm B normal-gen") suggests Sauers' manuscript was still being prepared for arXiv and that there is a credit/priority dispute with Eckhardt. [GitHub issue](https://github.com/SauersML/group-approximation/issues/191)
- A possible route to finite presentation: Fournier-Facio's paper (2608.02025) notes that being non-sofic is an *open* property in the space of marked groups, which lets you get finitely presented non-sofic groups. I found no source showing the same argument works for non-MF. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2608.02025)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-29: Manifold's companion market on a non-hyperlinear group being proved in September was at about 85%. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/user496577185415897490191/will-a-nonhyperlinear-group-be-prov)
- 2026-09-25: A Proofs and Prompts blog post gives the timeline. On 13-14 August, Sauers and Eckhardt each independently found a non-MF group using ChatGPT 5.6 Sol, and the two constructions were very similar. Eckhardt's example is a Kun-Thom style wreath product; Sauers' embeds into a central extension of one. Eckhardt has since posted a revised arXiv version. On 20 September, Liu reportedly found a non-hyperlinear group. [Proofs and Prompts](https://proofsandprompts.com/2026/09/25/from-non-sofic-to-non-hyperlinear-groups-the-new-messiness-of-discovering-and-announcing-big-results/)
- 2026-09: A conditional construction of a non-hyperlinear group was posted (arXiv 2609.27795). [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2609.27795)
- 2026-08-17/18: Tech Insider reported Manifold traders at 70%, then 95%, on a non-MF proof that month. It also said no non-MF group was publicly known at that point. [Tech Insider 95%](https://tech-insider.org/non-mf-group-manifold-market-95-percent-astra-ai/), [Tech Insider 70%](https://tech-insider.org/non-mf-group-prediction-market-manifold-astra-bet/)
- 2026-08: Kun and Thom, "Nonsofic wreath products of residually finite groups" (2608.06222), builds on OpenAI's non-sofic group. This is the template the non-MF constructions follow. [arXiv](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06222)
- 2026-08-01: OpenAI announced the first non-sofic group. [Ground Truth](https://groundtruth.day/news/the-non-sofic-group-is-the-openai-claim-a-computer-can-check.html)

## 4. Base rates
- Until August 2026, no non-MF group was known, even though the problem had been open for decades. A March 2026 paper describes few known non-amenable MF examples, and earlier literature says there are "no known examples" of non-MF groups. [Shulman 2603.13564](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2603.13564), [arXiv 2306.02498](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2306.02498)
- In August-September 2026 several related problems (non-sofic, non-MF, possibly non-hyperlinear) fell within weeks of each other, all with AI assistance. So the usual historical base rate says little here.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Manifold, this market: 70% to 95% in mid-August, according to Tech Insider. I could not see the current price.
- Manifold, the related non-hyperlinear market: about 85% on 2026-09-29.
- I found no Polymarket or Kalshi markets.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (around 2026-10-11)
- The creator's resolution decision. The key judgement calls are whether "finitely presented" will be enforced strictly, and whether the August work by Eckhardt and Sauers counts as "generally considered valid".
- Sauers' manuscript may appear on arXiv (issue #191 points to an imminent posting), and Eckhardt's revisions or expert commentary could follow.
- Any note showing a finitely presented non-MF group, for example by an openness argument like the one used for non-sofic groups.

ted as settled.
  - The "finitely presented" requirement probably follows formally. MF passes to subgroups, since the full C*-algebra of a subgroup embeds in that of the group.
